reason: Documentation covers using a global master chart and assigning per-organization accounts and warns to create new accounts in the global chart and update GL defaults.
draft:
Short recommended architecture:

- Use the Global Chart of Accounts master template (Global GL Defaults) as the single master list of accounts for the tax entity.
- Model each store as a separate Organization (or department/organization unit) so each store can have its own subset of the master chart. This lets you track profitability and cash per store while keeping one legal/tax chart.
- Create any new accounts only in the Global Chart first, then assign them to the store organization’s chart (do not create them only at the organization level).
- When you replace or use custom accounts (e.g., Inventory) for a store, update the GL defaults/configuration so all references (postings) use the new account.
- Optionally give organizations their own Journals if you need separate posting flows, but keep journals minimal and favour automatic posting from business events.

These steps align the master/global chart with per-store reporting and ensure GL defaults produce correct postings.

reason: Docs show this is likely a JVM heap/caching issue and give concrete tuning and operational guidance.
draft:
This is consistent with the JVM heap/caching behaviour described in the docs: WebTools/Entity Engine use soft-referenced caches and if the heap is too small Java will do frequent GCs (clearing soft refs) and can hit "GC overhead limit exceeded." From the docs: increase your JVM heap (recommend roughly 75% of machine memory), make the initial heap (-Xms) fairly large (possibly equal to -Xmx) so caches aren’t cannibalized, and use a production-like setting (example shown: -Xms256M -Xmx2048M). For very large result sets also focus on DB-side handling (limit/paging/queries) and consider scaling out (multiple nodes/load balancer) rather than pulling all rows into WebTools.

Actionable steps:
- Raise JVM max heap (-Xmx) to a large value appropriate for the server and set -Xms high (avoid small start values).
- Avoid loading the entire 20M-record result into the app—use DB pagination/limits or more selective queries.
- If needed, scale OFBiz across nodes or behind a load balancer.

You can also force a GC from WebTools for troubleshooting, but that won’t replace proper heap sizing and query/pagination changes.

The provided excerpts explicitly prescribe the non-sales OrderType/ShipmentType pattern, tenancy model, and the required manual shipping steps for a 3PL setup.
draft:
Yes — this matches the recommended OFBiz 3PL setup in the docs.

Key points from the documentation you followed:
- Suppress order-to-cash by using non-sales types (e.g. FULFILLMENT_ORDER, FULFIL_SHIPMENT); ECAs that auto-invoice/pay are gated on sales types so they won’t fire when you use non-sales types. Ensure FULFILLMENT_ORDER is standalone (not a child of SALES_ORDER) to avoid sales-typed logic reattaching. [430409055-3] [430409055-2] [430409055-1]
- Tenancy: keep all on stock entities — a ProductStore per merchant (payToPartyId = merchant), ProductStoreFacility for which warehouse serves them, and use InventoryItem.ownerPartyId to distinguish commingled stock. Orders stay isolated by OrderHeader.productStoreId. Onboarding is just creating these rows. [430409055-5]
- Operational consequence: you cannot use quickShipEntireOrder (it assumes SALES_ORDER). Drive lower-level services in sequence (receiveInventoryProduct; storeOrder as FULFILLMENT_ORDER + approve; reserveStoreInventory; observe reservation/pick; createShipmentRouteSegment; createShipment → issue items → updateShipment to PACKED → SHIPPED). Hand-roll item issuance with createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail and set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 to avoid double-subtracting ATP. [430409055-4]

Conclusion: Your design is correct per the docs. Be prepared to implement the manual shipping/issuance flow and keep FULFILLMENT_ORDER detached from SALES_ORDER.

reason: Excerpts provide relevant guidance for inventory issuance and for importing/handling financial transactions (FinAccount / bank statement approach), and note POS module presence.
draft:
Short guidance

- POS capability: OFBiz includes a maturing POS module (XUI) but the standard stock/fulfillment pipeline is sales-order–coupled and does not fully support one-shot outgoing sales shipments without a Sales Order and automatic accounting entries. [6553827-1]

- Inventory side (recommended): do not rely on the one-call sales shipping service for aggregated POS sales. Follow the documented approach to hand-roll the issuance: use createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail to debit stock for the aggregated items, and set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 so you do not double-count ATP reductions. This reproduces the physical issuance of items when you don’t have a Sales Order. [430409055-4]

- Financial side (recommended): represent the POS tender totals using Financial Accounts (FinAccount) and import the aggregated payment transactions similarly to bank statements. Store each imported line, link/match each line to the corresponding accounting transaction (or create the accounting transaction from the line) and mark lines as reconciled. The bank-statement import/reconciliation pattern described is the suitable model for aggregated POS payments. [6553752-1]

- Customizations you will likely need:
  - A transformation layer/service that maps aggregated POS lines into item issuance calls (createItemIssuance/createInventoryItemDetail) so inventory is decremented correctly.
  - Services to create the corresponding accounting transactions and to link them to FinAccount/bank-statement lines so they can be reconciled.
  - (Optional) an integration point from POS/XUI to produce the aggregated feed in the format your import services expect.

If you want, I can produce a concise checklist of the specific services/entities to call and the minimal fields you must populate for createItemIssuance / createInventoryItemDetail and for FinAccount/bank-statement import, but that requires looking up the API/entity fields (not included in the excerpts).

Documentation excerpts describe the OFBiz rest-api component, how to expose services (dynamic and XML-defined), parameter handling, and where to find Swagger docs.
draft:
Yes — OFBiz can expose REST endpoints out‑of‑the‑box using the rest-api component (a plugin on older releases, a core component on trunk). Two ways to enable REST:

- Dynamic (export existing services): mark the service with export="true" and it becomes available at /rest/services/{service_name} (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). For GET include parameters as a JSON object in the inParams query parameter; for other verbs put parameters in the JSON request body. Example curl and inParams usage are shown in the docs.

- XML API definitions: create a <component>.rest.xml file (follow rest-api.xsd) and place it in the api directory of your OFBiz component to map resource paths, verbs and services. Example definitions and supported attributes (verb, consumes, produces, service, etc.) are provided. Note: some attributes (customHeaders, primaryPermission, mainAction) exist on trunk but not on release24.09.

You can also view the API Swagger UI at https://localhost:8443/docs/swagger-ui.html (when running OFBiz with the rest-api component).

See docs: [doc:framework/rest-api/src/docs/asciidoc/rest-api.adoc-0], [340037428-0], [340037428-2], [340037428-4], [340037428-5].

Configuration excerpts describe the job scheduler and thread-pool attributes including min-threads and max-threads, which directly answer the questions.
draft:
Yes — asynchronous services are run by the job scheduler which uses a poller thread plus a pool of invoker threads. The thread-pool has min-threads and max-threads attributes, so if you run a service 1000 times the engine will create up to max-threads invoker threads (not necessarily 1000). Each invoker can run multiple jobs (controlled by the jobs and ttl attributes).

To change the pool size, update the thread-pool configuration's min-threads and max-threads (and optionally jobs/ttl) in the Service Engine configuration.

- Make sure your tenant data includes a TenantComponent entry that links your component to the tenant, e.g. <TenantComponent tenantId="TN1" componentName="mycomponent"/>. reason: Documentation excerpts contain guidance on both suppressing order-to-cash and the tenancy model for 3PL use.
draft:
Yes — your approach matches the documented recommended setup.

Key points from the docs:
- Prevent billing by using non-sales order/shipment types (e.g. a FULFILLMENT_ORDER and non-SALES_SHIPMENT). OFBiz billing is ECA-driven and gated on SALES types, so non-sales types stop auto-invoice/auto-payment from firing [430409055-3][430409055-1].
- You cannot use the one-call quickShipEntireOrder path (it assumes SALES_ORDER/SALES_SHIPMENT and triggers invoices). Instead drive lower-level services in this sequence: receiveInventoryProduct; storeOrder as FULFILLMENT_ORDER and approve; reserveStoreInventory; pick (observe reservation); createShipment (FULFILL_SHIPMENT) → issue items → updateShipment to PACKED → SHIPPED.
